content:
The image shows a corn leaf with:
- Numerous small, dark (black/dark brown), oval to circular lesions scattered densely across the leaf surface
- Some larger tan/brown irregular necrotic patches interspersed
- A yellowish midrib running diagonally
- Leaf has a greenish-gray cast overall

The key diagnostic feature is the small, raised, tar-like black spots scattered across the leaf — these are the characteristic stromata of *Phyllachora maydis*. Some lesions also show the "fisheye" pattern (dark center + tan halo) typical of tar spot complex. No rust pustules, no elongated blight lesions, no mosaic/streak patterning.
